row.team_price_text: No plans; pay for ads delivered (no minimum budget)
row.evidence: X's Ads API docs say advertisers grant other X @usernames access to their X Ads account "via the X UI at business.x.com", each with an account-level permission; no SCIM endpoint or SAML SSO appears anywhere in the X developer documentation.
row.notes: Twitter Ads now sells as X Ads. Ads accounts are reached through personal X user accounts; admins add other X @usernames in Ads Manager (multi-user login) with roles such as Account administrator, Ad manager, Campaign analyst, Organic analyst and Creative Manager. No SCIM, no enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO and no user-management API: the Ads API only lets the signed-in user read their own permissions (authenticated_user_access). No plans or seats; advertisers pay only for ads that run, so plan and price fields are empty. The X Help Center (multi-user login FAQ) refused every fetch. Status none is by absence (rule 5): the full docs.x.com text export contains no SCIM or SAML mention.

scim.notes: By absence (rule 5): access is granted per X @username in the Ads UI; no SCIM endpoint is documented.

endpoints.purpose: Read the authenticated user's permissions on an ads account (read-only)

user_api.notes: The Ads API (OAuth 1.0a, REST at ads-api.x.com) manages campaigns, not users. The only user-access endpoint reads the current user's own permissions; adding or removing users is an Account administrator action in the UI.
